answer.honda: VIN encodes it for every model year from 1984 on: character 6 for MY1984-1986, character 7 (odd digit = manual) for MY1987-2009, character 7 (A/C/E/G = manual) for MY2010 on.
answer.acura: VIN encodes it for every model year (1986 on): character 7, odd digit = manual for MY1986-2009, A/C/E/G = manual for MY2010 on.
answer.vpic_already_decodes_it: vPIC already turns this code into TransmissionStyle for almost every Honda/Acura VIN (Honda 21,026 and Acura 3,534 lot cars have a vPIC transmission), so the rules newly reach only the few cars where vPIC is blank or the VIN is not in the decode cache. Their larger value is correcting vPIC where it contradicts Honda's own table (vpic_conflicts).

vin_scheme.positions: 1-3 WMI; 4-8 Honda 'model code' (4-5 line, 6 line/engine, 7 body + transmission, 8 grade); 9 check digit; 10 model year; 11 plant; 12-17 serial

vin_regex_note: Each rule's vin_regex checks the WMI, the transmission character and the character-10 year code. Character 10 letters repeat every 30 years (A = 1980 or 2010), so the model year is resolved with the listing/vPIC year (scope.model_years); the check digit is verified separately; the 'not in vPIC' split and the 1997 Accord carve-out need the extra conditions stated in the rule.
not_encoded_or_not_ruled: Honda MY1981-1983: not ruled. The earliest Honda filings in NHTSA's MID are from August 1983 (MY1984). vPIC's decodes for the 7 MY1981-83 Hondas on the lots are consistent with the MY1984 layout (character 6 = transmission), but no Honda document for those years was found, so no rule covers them.

Honda MY1984 Civic hatchback/CRX/sedan (line codes AF, AG, AH, AK): not ruled for 1984. The MY1984 filing in MID covers only Accord, Prelude and Civic Wagon; the Civic hatchback/sedan table for 1984 was not found (1985 and 1986 tables were).
Honda Passport (1994-2002, WMI 4S6) and Acura SLX (1996-99, WMI JAE) are Isuzu-built and use Isuzu's VIN layout; Honda's character-7 code does not apply and no rule here covers them.

Honda/Acura VINs whose character 7 is outside the table for the era (e.g. a letter on a 2001-2009 VIN or a digit on a 2010+ VIN) are not ruled; on the lots they are listing-year errors or mis-typed VINs.

The code says manual vs automatic, not the gear count or the gearbox model; speeds stay with vPIC/EPA. Automatic codes cover CVT and DCT as well (e.g. 2015+ TLX 'F' = 8-speed DCT or 9-speed automatic).
Cars without a VIN (Honda 2,699, Acura 426 on the lots) cannot be reached by these rules.

Held, not ruled (verification 2026-11-05): Canada-only Acura EL (MB4 1997-2000, ES3 2001-05) and CSX (FD5/FD6 2006-11) codes. Their line codes are in no Honda filing and vPIC rejects the VINs, so the character-7 reading is pattern-only (honda_acura_vin7_code_not_in_vpic_*, status hold_code_not_filed).

conditions: VIN is 17 characters and its check digit (character 9) is valid (49 CFR 565.15(c)); VINs that fail it are skipped, not guessed

character-7 rules: characters 4-7 for that model year are a code NHTSA's vPIC decodes to a model (the VIN's own decode has a Model, or another VIN of that year in the decode cache, lot or departed, with the same characters 4-7 does); codes vPIC does not know go to honda_acura_vin7_code_not_in_vpic_* (held)

validation_method: For each rule, every lot car in scope is matched by WMI, valid check digit, VIN model year and the character-6/7 value. 'checkable' = its ground_truth.jsonl line has class manual/automatic/cvt/amt/dct and uniformCell is empty (uniform-cell lines are vPIC model-level defaults and are counted separately as unlabelled). Agreement = same manual-vs-not-manual answer. All VIN-bearing ground truth comes from vPIC, which NHTSA builds from these same Honda filings, so agreement is partly circular; the EPA cross-check (does EPA list a transmission of the claimed kind for that year/make/model, narrowed to the vPIC displacement when known) is the independent check. 'newly_confirmed_manual' = in-scope cars whose published extras transmission is empty today.
